header: Reading a health check-up schedule, checking it against HR and storing it is ONE definition here, used by the circular UPLOAD (so a schedule is ready the moment its circular is saved, with nobody running anything) and by scripts/import-health-checkups.ts (dry runs, reports, a re-import by hand). They cannot disagree, because they are the same code. I pass in everything outside the logic (the Gemini readers, the database), so it is tested without a network. My rules (the same whoever calls):

* A schedule is STORED only if nothing looked wrong: no problems at all (a row without a date, a group of an odd size, dates out of order, a month that could not be read, no rows). Anything else is reported and left for a person (the import tool shows why); the circular itself is never affected.
* Storing REPLACES the circular's rows (delete + insert), so reading the same circular again gives the same result, never doubled rows.
* Running out of time is not a failure of the circular: the caller saves the circular and the schedule is read later by the tool.

symbols.name: Sql
doc: Runs one SQL statement and returns its rows. An EntityManager, a pg client or a test double can all be adapted to this.

symbols.name: InTransaction
doc: Runs `fn` inside one database transaction: BEGIN ... COMMIT, and ROLLBACK if it throws.

symbols.name: loadHrContext
symbols.sig: export async function loadHrContext(sql: Sql): Promise<HrContext>
doc: I load the HR directory (EVERYONE, not only non-executives: a person on an old roster may have been promoted since and is still the same person) and which department code belongs to which department name (used to check the codes read from the pages).

members.name: groups
members.type: Array<{ date: string | null; rows: number }>

members.name: codeFixes
doc: Rows whose department code I changed because it did not belong to the department printed on the row.

members.name: problems
doc: Anything that looked wrong. I do not store the schedule while this is not empty.

members.name: counts
members.type: { verified: number; corrected: number; unverified: number }

symbols.name: prepareSchedule
symbols.sig: export async function prepareSchedule(extracted: ExtractedSchedule, ctx: HrContext, sql: Sql): Promise<PreparedSchedule>
doc: Checks every row: the department code against the printed department, then the people against HR. I read the HR phonetic codes of the printed names from the database.

symbols.name: scheduleVerdict
symbols.sig: export function scheduleVerdict(p: PreparedSchedule): { apply: boolean; problems: string[] }
doc: My one rule for storing: only a schedule with no problems at all.

symbols.name: storeSchedule
symbols.sig: export async function storeSchedule(sql: Sql, circularId: number, p: PreparedSchedule): Promise<void>
doc: I replace the circular's rows in public.health_checkup_schedule (delete, then insert in batches); the caller owns the transaction.

members.name: prepared
doc: Present when the pages were read and checked (status ready or needs-review).

symbols.name: runScheduleStage
symbols.sig: export async function runScheduleStage(args: { pages: Buffer[]; sql: Sql; deadlineAt: number; readers?: RosterReaders; hr?: HrContext; extract?: (pages: Buffer[], deps: { readers: RosterReaders; shouldStop?: () => boolean }) => Promise<ExtractedSchedule>; }): Promise<ScheduleStage>

params.name: args
params.type: { pages: Buffer[]; sql: Sql; deadlineAt: number; readers?: RosterReaders; hr?: HrContext; extract?: (pages: Buffer[], deps: { readers: RosterReaders; shouldStop?: () => boolean }) => Promise<ExtractedSchedule>; }

doc: I read the schedule from the circular's pages and check it, WITHOUT storing anything. This never throws: whatever happens, the caller gets a status (ready / needs-review / timeout / failed) and saves the circular regardless. pages every page image of the circular, in order (so page numbers are the circular's real page numbers; pages that are not rosters are skipped) deadlineAt Date.now() value after which the reading stops with status "timeout" readers the two Gemini readers (a primary and a checker); created from the environment when not given

symbols.name: applyScheduleStage
symbols.sig: export async function applyScheduleStage(inTransaction: InTransaction, circularId: number, stage: ScheduleStage): Promise<{ stored: number }>
doc: Stores a ready schedule in its own transaction. I throw if the stage is not ready or the database refuses; the caller logs it and the circular stays.

symbols.name: stageDetail
symbols.sig: export function stageDetail(stage: ScheduleStage, rosterPages: number[]): Record<string, unknown>
doc: What a stage found, in a form for the log. I keep it small: never the rows themselves.

symbols.name: logIngest
symbols.sig: export async function logIngest(sql: Sql, circularId: number, kind: IngestKind, status: IngestStatus, detail: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<boolean>
doc: Writes what the upload decided. Best effort: I never want the log to be the reason an upload fails (the table may not exist yet). Returns whether it was written.

behaviours: the HR directory and the department list are loaded from the database (4 people, 4 department code -> name pairs)
four people who are in HR with the right names: all verified, no problems, and the verdict is to store
a department code that does not belong to the printed department is corrected (32004 -> 32001), and a person HR does not know stays UNVERIFIED (kept, flagged)
...an unverified person is NOT a problem: the schedule is still stored (it is flagged, not dropped)
a warning from the reading (a group of an odd size) is a problem: NOT stored
a month that could not be read is a problem: NOT stored
no rows at all is a problem: NOT stored
storing writes the rows; storing the SAME circular again REPLACES them (4, then still 4: never doubled)
the stored row is what the answers read: ticket, name, code, department, date, circular label from the circular, id and page
a schedule whose month is unknown cannot be stored at all (and the earlier rows are untouched)
a good reading: status ready, with the prepared rows (nothing is stored yet)
a reading with a problem: status needs-review, the problems are listed, the rows are prepared but the stage says not to store
running out of time: status timeout, and it does not throw
any other failure: status failed with the first line of the error, and it does not throw
the reading is told to stop once the deadline has passed (and not before)
a ready stage is stored in its own transaction: 4 rows for circular 8
a stage that is not ready is REFUSED (never stored by accident)
if storing fails half way (the delete happened, the insert did not) everything is rolled back: the earlier 4 rows are still there
the log detail is small and useful: roster pages, seconds, month, rows, days, counts, problems; and never the rows themselves
a stage that failed is logged with its error
a log entry is written
...with its kind, its status and its detail as JSON
if the log table does not exist yet, logging returns false and throws nothing (an upload never fails because of its log)
deleting a circular deletes its schedule rows AND its log: a re-upload starts clean
...and another circular's rows and log are untouched
the same circular uploaded again (a new id, the same serial and year) is ready at once with the same label: 'Circular 003 (2024)', 4 rows
